A.explanation: Gives about $1130 \text{ Pa}$ from $\rho h$ with $h = 0.10 \text{ m}$, omitting multiplication by $g$ and using the smallest height.

B.explanation: About ten times too small, from an error converting areas in $\text{cm}^2$ to $\text{m}^2$ when using $p = F/A$.

C.explanation: Gives about $11.1 \text{ kPa}$ from $p = \rho g h$ with $h = 0.10 \text{ m}$, which is the minimum pressure on the largest face.

D.explanation: Gives about $1.66 \times 10^4 \text{ Pa}$ from $p = \rho g h$ with the largest height $0.150 \text{ m}$ on the smallest face.

hints: Notice the word maximum: pressure is $p = F/A$, so for the same weight you need the smallest contact area from the $12.0 \text{ cm}$, $15.0 \text{ cm}$ and $10.0 \text{ cm}$ faces.
Connect weight to density: $F = mg$ and $m = \rho V$, so $p = \rho V g / A$ where $V$ is the block volume and $A$ is the chosen base area.

Use the shortcut $p = \rho g h$ where $h$ is the vertical height; for maximum pressure $h$ must be the longest side $15.0 \text{ cm} = 0.150 \text{ m}$ with $\rho = 1.13 \times 10^4 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
walkthrough: Find the weight, which is the same however the block sits. Volume $V = 0.120 \times 0.150 \times 0.100 = 1.80 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$, so mass $m = \rho V = 1.13 \times 10^4 \times 1.80 \times 10^{-3} = 20.3 \text{ kg}$.
State the pressure rule $p = F/A$ with $F = mg$. Maximum $p$ needs minimum contact area $A$.

The three face areas are $0.120 \times 0.150$, $0.150 \times 0.100$ and $0.120 \times 0.100 \text{ m}^2$. The smallest is $A_{min} = 0.120 \times 0.100 = 0.0120 \text{ m}^2$, so the $0.150 \text{ m}$ side is vertical.
Calculate $F = mg = 20.3 \times 9.81 = 199 \text{ N}$ and $p_{max} = F/A_{min} = 199 / 0.0120 = 1.66 \times 10^4 \text{ Pa}$.
Equivalently $p_{max} = \rho g h_{max} = 1.13 \times 10^4 \times 9.81 \times 0.150 = 1.66 \times 10^4 \text{ Pa} = 16.6 \text{ kPa}$, with correct pressure units. This is option D.
